records.title: LearnWithHupe: what it is
records.content: LearnWithHupe (Hupe Academy) is a curriculum-based learning app for children aged 2 to 8. It is live on Google Play and the App Store. The company published it about two months before Nov 2026 and has not started marketing it yet, so usage is still small. It was built at Carina Softlabs with a Flutter mobile app (by a separate Flutter developer), Phaser.js games, an Express backend and a React admin panel. Sreerag has worked on it from Feb to Sep 2026: the first build until late May, then about a month on the Phaser games, then admin, promo-code and billing work until mid Sep. Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hupe.hupe_academy_app. App Store: https://apps.apple.com/pl/app/learn-with-hupe/id6760534126.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: accounts and content
records.content: A parent is the main user. A parent can add up to 10 children, each with a name, an age and an avatar, and the children are kept apart by sessions. Each child has their own progress. Parents sign in with email, Google or Apple. Content follows a hierarchy: subject, then topics, then games and interactive activities.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: what Sreerag built
records.content: Sreerag built the LearnWithHupe backend: authentication and roles for parents and children, Google and Apple sign-in, the child profiles and progress tracking, the subscription billing integration with Google Play and the App Store, and a modular Express backend with more than 120 REST endpoints (about 60 of them for the admin panel). He also built the React, TypeScript and Vite admin panel for managing the curriculum (draft, published and archived states), and he runs the AWS servers (EC2, S3, Nginx, PM2) and the store consoles. A teammate built the Flutter mobile app.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: the Phaser games
records.content: Sreerag built the interactive games for LearnWithHupe with Phaser.js. The games are exported as HTML and shown inside the Flutter app. Phaser was suggested because the games stay under 1 MB and are very interactive. The games took about a month (around Jun 2026).

records.title: LearnWithHupe: cutting text-to-speech cost
records.content: The app uses ElevenLabs text-to-speech for voices. At first it called the API live, and it worked well, but the billing was very high. So Sreerag generated the voices once with a script, stored the audio on the server and in an S3 bucket, and played it back directly as Base64. This removed the repeated per-request cost and made playback easy.

records.title: LearnWithHupe billing: the store is the source of truth
records.content: For subscriptions, Sreerag treats Google Play and the App Store as the source of truth, not the app and not a webhook. A store notification only triggers a re-check against the store's server API. A scheduled check also re-verifies subscriptions that have gone stale: ones in a grace period or in billing retry are re-checked when they have gone 6 hours without verification, because a stale row there is lost revenue, and active or trial ones after 24 hours, because they change rarely. A dropped notification can therefore leave an active subscription wrongly entitled for up to about 25 hours, which was a deliberate business trade-off. This keeps the backend correct when renewals, cancellations or refunds happen outside the app.

records.title: LearnWithHupe billing: Google plan-change token lineage
records.content: When a subscriber changes plan, Google Play issues a new purchase token. Treating it as a brand new purchase lost the link to the original subscriber. Sreerag resolves the lineage between the old and new tokens, so ownership carries across plan changes.

records.title: LearnWithHupe billing: fixing a duplicate-notification race
records.content: Two notifications for the same purchase could arrive at nearly the same time. The second one hit a duplicate-key error, and the code read that as "this purchase belongs to another account", which wrongly rejected a legitimate purchase. Sreerag changed the handling to tell a harmless same-owner race apart from a real ownership conflict, and added regression tests.

records.title: LearnWithHupe billing: store outages versus rejected purchases
records.content: Store outages used to look like failed purchases. Sreerag added a shared error mapper: a Google or Apple rate limit (429) or server error (5xx) becomes a retryable 503, and a genuinely rejected purchase stays a 400. The app can then retry later instead of telling the user their purchase failed.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: counting paying subscribers correctly
records.content: The admin dashboard once counted free trials as paying subscribers. Sreerag corrected the count to exclude trials, and wrote tests for older rows, trials that had just converted to paid, and lapsed grandfathered trials.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: safe sync and account deletion
records.content: Progress from one device is synced offline-first and applied to several children in a single transaction, so a partial write cannot corrupt a child's progress. Account deletion cascades across more than 7 collections with a self-expiring audit log, and keeps only hashed device fingerprints to stop repeated free trials. The deletion is built to follow GDPR-style rules, but it is not a legal compliance claim.

records.title: Warvox: what it is
records.content: Warvox is a public game website and multilingual content system for a game platform, built at Carina Softlabs. Sreerag worked on it from mid Nov 2025 to Feb 2026. It has game pages, a community forum, an admin panel and an automatic translation pipeline (English plus 10 translated languages, 11 in all). It is not publicly launched yet. The live address, playwarvox.com, shows an upcoming page for now, and the staging site, which has the current real content, is at playwarvox-staging.vercel.app.

records.title: Warvox: what Sreerag built
records.content: Sreerag built the Warvox website front end (Next.js), the backend with its admin APIs, the content system and the forum pages. The admin backend uses role-based access control. The backend creates the Stripe checkout on the server and verifies the webhook signature. The game itself was not his work.

records.title: Warvox: the 3D model viewer
records.content: Warvox shows 3D models such as swords, weapons and armour. Admins upload models of any size, shape and polygon count, and the site automatically centres and fits each one in the card, with zoom and rotate controls, similar to Sketchfab. Sreerag built this interactive viewer.

records.title: Warvox: the translation pipeline
records.content: Admins write content in English, and a background worker picks up translation tasks from a queue every few seconds and translates them with AWS Translate into 10 languages besides English (11 in all), including Arabic, which is written right to left. If a task fails, it is retried up to 3 times, and failures are counted on the translation job. Translations live in a separate collection from the English content, so the page can serve the requested language with a lang parameter. A content hash lets the pipeline skip fields that did not change.

records.title: HRMS: what it is

records.title: HRMS: dashboard and attendance behaviour

records.title: HRMS: policies and complaints

Each category holds PDFs, and a person must stay on a PDF for it to count as read. The complaints form takes a title, a recipient role (admin, management or HR) and a description, and sends the complaint straight to that role.

records.title: PM tool and Sales tool: what they are
records.content: The PM tool is Carina Softlabs' internal project management app. It connects to the company's Sales tool and HRMS. When the Sales tool wins a deal, the project can move into the PM tool without re-entering data. Project managers then plan milestones, sprints and tasks, and employees see their own work. HRMS provides people, leave, shifts and capacity. All three share one sign-in and role-based permissions. Sreerag worked on it from Aug to early Oct 2026. The back end is NestJS with MongoDB, with real-time updates over Socket.io (using a Redis adapter) and Firebase push notifications, and the PM tool and the Sales tool front ends are Next.js. It is a team project led by the Team Lead, and the company uses it.

records.title: PM tool: what Sreerag built
records.content: Sreerag worked full stack on the PM tool. He built the whole tasks module, the employee dashboard, the projects pages, milestones and sprints, and the notifications, from the front end to the backend. He also built project notifications in the Sales tool, with Firebase push notifications and sockets, and used the same approach in the PM tool.

records.title: PM tool: how a project moves
records.content: In the PM tool a project starts in a planning stage, and moves to ongoing only when it is ready: it needs milestones with dates, tasks with an owner, dates, an estimate and a priority, and a team. Milestones after the first can be locked until the project manager requests an unlock and the Sales side approves it. Tasks have statuses from new through in progress and in review to completed, and a review can send a task back for rework with a reason.

records.title: Carina Softlabs website and admin panel migration
records.content: In Oct 2026 Sreerag migrated the Carina Softlabs company website and its admin panel, alone, from Angular 16 to the latest Angular 22. He fixed a lot of old tangled code, and published the new version with server-side rendering (SSR), so the site is newer, more stable and faster. The new site is live at carinasoftlabs.com.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant (this site): what it is
records.content: This website is a portfolio you can talk to. Visitors ask questions and get streamed, cited answers grounded in Sreerag's portfolio. Visitors can also pick stored cards for his profile, projects, skills and contact. It was built to show a real, measured RAG system. Stack: retrieval-augmented generation with Gemini, a Qdrant vector database, a Cloudflare Worker backend with server-sent events, and a Next.js 16 front end with a water effect and liquid glass design. It was built with AI-assisted development (Claude Code). The source code is public on GitHub at github.com/sreeragpariyarath/ai-portfolio-assistant.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: retrieval and evaluation
records.content: Retrieval uses hybrid search: BM25 keyword search and dense vector search, combined with reciprocal rank fusion. On 73 development questions the hybrid search found the needed evidence in the top 10 results 98.6% of the time. A separate answer evaluation checked 73 answers with rules: no private content leaked, no injected instruction followed, the expected evidence cited 95.2% of the time and the right behaviour 93.2% of the time. These were development questions that the same author wrote, so they are not a held-out test.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: four answer behaviours
records.content: Every answer declares one of four behaviours: answer (the evidence supports it), qualify (the evidence is uncertain, old, conflicting or unverified, so say so), abstain (the evidence does not support an answer, so say so without guessing) and refuse (the request crosses a privacy or security line). Citations are checked, and any citation that was not actually retrieved is removed before the visitor sees it.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: keeping private data private
records.content: Privacy is enforced at three points: the keyword index is built only from public records, the vector search always uses a public-only filter, and a last check drops anything that is not in the public set before it reaches the prompt. Text found in records is treated as data, never as instructions, and a test record with a planted instruction checks that it is ignored.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: keeping it fast and reliable
records.content: It uses a per-visitor rate limit, an in-memory cache for repeated question embeddings, a fallback to a second Gemini model if the first one fails, and a friendly "demo busy" message. One Cloudflare Worker serves both the static site and the API.

records.title: Erris: what it is
records.content: Erris is a solo open source project by Sreerag: transport-neutral, type-safe error contracts for JavaScript and TypeScript, started in Aug 2026. It gives an application one typed vocabulary for failure. Four packages are published on npm: @erris/core, @erris/http, @erris/adapter-zod and @erris/adapter-prisma, all at version 1.0.2. A fifth package, @erris/express, is in progress and is not published yet. The code is on GitHub at github.com/sreeragpariyarath/erris and is MIT licensed. Releases are published from GitHub Actions with Changesets, using npm trusted publishing with provenance and no stored npm token. Download numbers so far are small.

records.title: Erris: how it is built and tested
records.content: Erris is built with TypeScript, pnpm, Vitest with type-level tests, and tsup. It has continuous integration on Node 22 and 24, CodeQL security scanning, Changesets for versioning, and a written design RFC (Erris-RFC-0001). The release workflow has the permissions that npm trusted publishing needs, and no stored npm token.

records.title: Erris: a core with no dependencies and no HTTP
records.content: The Erris core package has zero runtime dependencies and knows nothing about HTTP. HTTP status codes live in a separate package, @erris/http, and there is no global registry: a normaliser is configured per use. That way any framework or library can use the core without pulling in Express or a logger.

records.title: Erris: the field is called detail, not message
records.content: Erris errors use the fields code, status, title, detail and cause. The field is named detail, not message, to match RFC 9457 Problem Details, so the HTTP response needs no translation. It also avoids a clash with the built-in message field of JavaScript errors.

records.title: Norix CLI
records.content: Norix (npm package norix-cli) is a "repository intelligence" command line tool for Node.js projects, published by Sreerag around Aug 2026. It scans a repository offline and finds frameworks, databases, ORMs, validation libraries, authentication and queues. It also gives architecture insights, shows how parts of the system relate, flags project health issues and exports machine-readable reports. It is at version 1.16.2 with 5 releases and is MIT licensed. Usage is small so far (about 6 weekly and 26 monthly downloads in late Oct 2026). Source: github.com/sreeragpariyarath/norix.

records.title: Yexora IT Solutions website (client project)
records.content: Sreerag built the marketing website for Yexora IT Solutions as a freelance client project in Sep and Oct 2026. It is live at yexoraitsolutions.com. It is one scrolling page over a 3D fibre-light scene with liquid-glass panels, a works reel and a contact form. Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Three.js (react-three-fiber, drei and postprocessing) and Lenis smooth scrolling, exported as a static site on Cloudflare, with the videos served from Cloudflare R2 and the contact form sent through Web3Forms. There is no backend.

records.title: Open source and side projects
records.content: Outside work Sreerag builds open source and side projects: Erris (typed error contracts for JavaScript and TypeScript, solo, on npm), the Norix CLI (repository analysis, on npm), the Yexora IT Solutions client website, a personal tracker app, and this AI portfolio assistant.

records.title: All projects at a glance
records.content: Projects Sreerag has worked on: LearnWithHupe (children's learning app, live on Google Play and the App Store), Warvox (game website and multilingual content system, not launched yet), HRMS (internal HR platform), Upthrust (learning platform with CMS and LMS), the PM tool and Sales tool (internal project management and sales), the Carina Softlabs website and admin panel migration to Angular 22, Erris (open source error contracts), the Norix CLI, the Yexora IT Solutions website and this AI portfolio assistant.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: the admin panel
records.content: The LearnWithHupe admin panel is written in React 19, TypeScript and Vite. Staff manage the curriculum with a draft, published and archived workflow. It uses reusable components, compound database indexes and Redis caching, and it shows the number of paying subscribers.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: servers and operations
records.content: Sreerag runs the LearnWithHupe servers: AWS EC2 with Nginx and PM2, S3 and CloudFront for files, Cloudinary for media, Certbot for HTTPS and Winston for logs. He also manages the Google Play Console and Apple App Store Connect, and wrote the technical documentation.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: real-time features and activity uploads
records.content: The LearnWithHupe backend uses Socket.io for real-time features, and a file upload pipeline for ZIP packages of HTML learning activities. Access is controlled by roles and permissions stored in the database, and the API uses rate limiting and security hardening.

records.title: Warvox: forum and caching
records.content: The Warvox site has forum pages where players can interact and chat. Because the site is mostly static, data-heavy content, the front end caches the content it fetches in the browser (with SWR, for about three minutes) to keep it quick.

records.title: HRMS: the three portals
records.content: HRMS has three portals that share one sign-in: the HR portal for employees and HR, a Finance portal, and an Inventory portal for tracking company hardware such as laptops and phones. Sreerag's part was the employee-facing HR screens and some backend APIs.

records.title: HRMS: leave, calendar and SOP screens
records.content: The leaves page lets employees request leave and see leave taken. The calendar shows a month view where HR adds holidays and every employee can see them. The SOP page lists the company's standard operating procedures.

records.title: PM tool and Sales tool: notifications
records.content: Sreerag built the notification system end to end. In the Sales tool it sends project notifications with Firebase push notifications and sockets, and he used the same approach in the PM tool, where people get an inbox of events such as task assignments and review decisions.

records.title: PM tool: employee dashboard and project overview
records.content: The employee dashboard in the PM tool shows what needs doing today, what is overdue and what is coming up, the task the person is working on, task counts by status, capacity warnings and the projects they are on. The project overview page shows project health, milestone delivery, sprints, work by category and the team. Sreerag built both.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: the front end
records.content: The front end is a static Next.js 16 export with a one-screen home, a water effect on the home screen (a TypeScript port of an MIT-licensed fluid simulation), a liquid glass look, stored cards for profile, projects, skills and contact, and a streaming chat view with citations. It is tested with Playwright and axe accessibility checks. The home page loads about 197 KB of JavaScript, and on a desktop it ran at about 56 to 60 frames per second.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: how a question is answered
records.content: A question is checked for size and format, rate limited per visitor, turned into a vector (cached when repeated), and searched with hybrid search over the public records. The top 8 records go into a prompt as data. Gemini streams the answer, the answer is parsed for its behaviour and citations, invalid citations are removed, and the visitor gets the text, the behaviour and the cited sources.

records.title: AI portfolio assistant: current status and limits
records.content: The assistant is built and deployed: this site is the live version, running on Cloudflare Workers. Its evaluation so far used development questions written by its author, not a held-out test. It answers from Sreerag's real portfolio records. When it is very busy it can show a "demo busy" message.

records.title: Erris: the packages
records.content: Erris has five packages. @erris/core holds the typed error catalogue and the normaliser, with no runtime dependencies. @erris/http renders errors as RFC 9457 Problem Details responses. @erris/adapter-zod and @erris/adapter-prisma turn Zod and Prisma errors into the same typed error. @erris/express, an error-handling middleware, is in progress and not published yet.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: promo codes and campaigns
records.content: In Jul 2026 Sreerag built promo-code tracking for LearnWithHupe: a public link that records each click and redirects, a URL shortener, tracking of when an email was sent, bulk sending, and attributing a sign-up to the promo code that brought it. He also built campaign management in the admin panel, including allocating promo codes to users.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: admin analytics and subscription management
records.content: Between Jul and Sep 2026 Sreerag extended the LearnWithHupe admin panel with analytics: a Revenue vs User Growth chart with a summary header and timeframe filters, a platform insights widget, a live activity feed, and a trial conversion summary. He also built a subscription management page with a status guide, and the ability to filter subscribers by status and by join date. He also made the layouts work on mobile and tablet.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: App Store Server API and weekly plan
records.content: In Jul 2026 Sreerag migrated the LearnWithHupe iOS purchase handling to the App Store Server API, and added weekly plan pricing.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: re-checking subscriptions against the stores
records.content: In Sep 2026 Sreerag built and refined a job that re-checks subscriptions against Google Play and the App Store. It chooses what to re-check by how long ago a subscription was last verified, not by when its period ends. It works through the backlog in batches and reports what is left. Store notifications are matched against the whole chain of purchase tokens, and Android subscriptions are identified by their original token. A returned failure is treated as a failure, never as a success.

records.title: LearnWithHupe: account safety
records.content: In Sep 2026 Sreerag throttled the sign-in and credential endpoints of LearnWithHupe and stopped them from revealing which email addresses have accounts. He also made children's progress visible without a subscription, and made the backend check that a child belongs to the parent asking.

records.title: Short summary for recruiters
records.content: Sreerag P is a full stack engineer in Indore, India, working mainly in TypeScript and the MERN stack. He has about one year of full-time experience at Carina Softlabs (intern from Jul 2025, full-time from Sep 2025), plus freelance work since Dec 2023 and an internship at Medlare in 2024. He owns backend, admin panel and server work for production platforms, including LearnWithHupe, a children's learning app that is live on Google Play and the App Store. He also builds React, Next.js and Angular interfaces, uses AI coding tools every day, and built this RAG portfolio assistant. He is open to full stack developer roles and forward deployed engineer roles, and open to relocating.

records.title: How much experience does Sreerag have?
records.content: Sreerag describes it as about one year of full-time experience, with more before that. The path: he finished a 6-month MERN full stack course in Dec 2023 and started freelance full stack work the same month; he was a full stack intern at Medlare from Jul to Dec 2024; he joined Carina Softlabs as an intern in Jul 2025 and became a full-time Full Stack Developer in Sep 2025. So he has roughly one year as a full-time developer at a company, plus freelance and internship experience on top.

records.title: Is Sreerag stronger in backend or frontend?
records.content: Sreerag is a full stack engineer who leans toward backend and admin systems. In his own words he has spent most of his time owning backend systems end to end: REST APIs, role-based access control, payment and store integrations, and admin panels. The evidence: he built the LearnWithHupe backend (more than 120 REST endpoints, store subscription billing) and its admin panel, the Warvox backend with its admin APIs, backend APIs in HRMS, and full stack work on the PM tool. On the frontend he built the Upthrust website, the HRMS employee screens, the Yexora client website, the Carina Softlabs website migration to Angular 22, and the React admin panels. So both are real, with the heavier ownership on the backend.

records.title: Sreerag's main strengths
records.content: Main strengths shown in his work: backend APIs with role-based access control; payment and store subscription integrations (Google Play, App Store and Stripe); admin and CMS panels; real-time features with WebSockets and Socket.io; running servers on AWS and managing the store consoles; careful handling of money and data (store-as-source-of-truth billing, transactional progress sync); cost-aware decisions (cutting text-to-speech cost); a multilingual content pipeline; shipping to real users; and open source packages with tests and automated releases. He also uses AI coding tools every day.

records.title: What from Sreerag's background fits forward deployed engineer roles?
records.content: Sreerag is looking for forward deployed engineer roles that involve AI. Parts of his background that relate: as a freelancer he works from requirements to deployment for clients; he runs deployments and the store consoles himself; he builds AI features (this RAG assistant with Gemini, Qdrant and an evaluation); he works across backend, frontend and servers; and he writes documentation and has mentored three interns. These are facts from his records, not a claim about any one job.

records.title: Which companies has Sreerag worked for?
records.content: The companies and clients Sreerag names: Carina Softlabs in Indore (since Jul 2025, intern then full-time Full Stack Developer), Medlare in Indore (full stack developer intern, Jul to Dec 2024), and freelance clients since Dec 2023 (the public example is the Yexora IT Solutions website; he does not name other clients publicly). He has not named any other employer. He is at the start of his career, with about one year of full-time experience.

records.title: What Sreerag built alone and what was team work
records.content: Built alone: Upthrust (website, backend, CMS and LMS), the Carina Softlabs website and admin panel migration to Angular 22, Erris, the Norix CLI, the Yexora website, and this assistant. Team work where he owned a clear part: LearnWithHupe (he owns the backend, billing, admin panel and servers; a teammate built the Flutter app), Warvox (he built the website front end, backend and content system; the game was not his work), HRMS (a team project; he built the employee screens and some backend APIs), and the PM tool and Sales tool (a team project led by the Team Lead; he built the tasks module, dashboard, projects pages, milestones, sprints and notifications).

records.title: Limits and honest notes about Sreerag's experience
records.content: Things he says openly: he is not a Flutter specialist (a separate Flutter developer built the LearnWithHupe app); the Warvox game was not his work; Warvox is not publicly launched yet; LearnWithHupe is live but its marketing has not started, so usage is still small; HRMS and the PM tool are team projects; the company repositories are private and cannot be shared; Erris and Norix have small download numbers so far and the Erris Express package is not published yet; he has no master's degree; and the evaluation of this assistant used development questions written by its author, not a held-out test. He has about one year of full-time experience.

records.title: Which of Sreerag's projects are public and which are private?
records.content: Public with source code: Erris (github.com/sreeragpariyarath/erris and npm, MIT licensed), the Norix CLI (github.com/sreeragpariyarath/norix and npm) and this assistant (github.com/sreeragpariyarath/ai-portfolio-assistant). Public to visit: LearnWithHupe on Google Play and the App Store, theupthrust.com, carinasoftlabs.com, yexoraitsolutions.com, and Warvox (an upcoming page at playwarvox.com, and a staging site). Private: the Carina Softlabs company repositories (LearnWithHupe, Warvox, HRMS, Upthrust, the PM tool and Sales tool) cannot be shared, HRMS and the PM tool are internal tools with no public address, and his personal tracker app is private.

records.title: Where has Sreerag used React?
records.content: React is a main tool for Sreerag. He built the LearnWithHupe admin panel with React 19, TypeScript and Vite; the interactive Upthrust website; the HRMS employee screens; the Yexora IT Solutions website (React 19 with Next.js 16 and Three.js); the React front end features at his Medlare internship; and he used React and Next.js for the PM tool and Sales tool front ends and for this assistant's front end.

records.title: Where has Sreerag used Next.js?
records.content: Sreerag used Next.js for the Warvox website front end, the PM tool and Sales tool front ends, the Yexora IT Solutions website (Next.js 16, exported as a static site), and this AI portfolio assistant (Next.js 16 as a static export with a water effect and liquid glass design).

records.title: Where has Sreerag used Angular?
records.content: In Oct 2026 Sreerag migrated the Carina Softlabs company website and its admin panel, alone, from Angular 16 to Angular 22. He cleaned up a lot of old tangled code and published the new version with server-side rendering (SSR). The site is live at carinasoftlabs.com. His main frameworks are still React and Next.js; Angular is a skill he has used in production.

records.title: Where has Sreerag used Node.js and Express?
records.content: Node.js and Express are the base of his backend work: the LearnWithHupe backend (a modular Express backend with more than 120 REST endpoints), the Warvox backend and its admin APIs, backend APIs for HRMS (complaints, policies and the employee profile), the Upthrust backend, and REST APIs at his Medlare internship.

records.title: Where has Sreerag used NestJS?
records.content: Sreerag used NestJS in the PM tool and Sales tool backend at Carina Softlabs (NestJS with MongoDB, real-time updates over Socket.io with a Redis adapter, and Firebase push notifications). It is a team project led by the Team Lead; Sreerag built the tasks module, the employee dashboard, the projects pages, milestones, sprints and the notifications, full stack.

records.title: Where has Sreerag used MongoDB and Redis?
records.content: MongoDB: the LearnWithHupe backend (Atlas, compound indexes, transactions for progress sync) and the PM tool backend. Redis: caching in the LearnWithHupe admin panel, and as the Socket.io adapter in the PM tool backend. (The Warvox website caches in the browser with SWR; Redis is not used there.) He also lists PostgreSQL as a skill, and he used Qdrant for vector search in this assistant.

records.title: What real-time features has Sreerag built?
records.content: Real-time work: live notifications over WebSockets in the HRMS dashboard; Socket.io real-time features in the LearnWithHupe backend; and in the PM tool and Sales tool, project notifications with Firebase push notifications and sockets (the backend uses Socket.io with a Redis adapter), including an inbox for events such as task assignments and review decisions. He built the notification system end to end.

records.title: What payment and subscription work has Sreerag done?
records.content: Payments and subscriptions: for LearnWithHupe he built the subscription billing backend for Google Play and the App Store, including re-checking subscriptions against the stores, plan changes, a migration to the App Store Server API, weekly plan pricing and promo codes. For Warvox, the backend creates the Stripe checkout on the server and verifies the webhook signature. He treats the store or payment provider as the source of truth.

records.title: What security work has Sreerag done?
records.content: Security work: role-based access control in several backends; JWT and refresh tokens, bcrypt and Google and Apple sign-in; webhook signature verification; rate limiting and Helmet; in LearnWithHupe, throttled sign-in endpoints that do not reveal which emails have accounts, a check that a child belongs to the parent asking, and account deletion across more than 7 collections (GDPR-style, not a legal compliance claim); and in this assistant, private records excluded at three layers and a defence against prompt injection. CodeQL scanning runs in the CI of Erris.

records.title: How does Sreerag test his code?
records.content: Testing: Erris uses Vitest with type-level tests, CI on Node 22 and 24 and CodeQL scanning. In LearnWithHupe he wrote regression tests for billing fixes, such as the duplicate-notification race and the paying-subscriber count. This assistant has unit tests, Playwright browser tests with axe accessibility checks, and an evaluation with measured results. His skills list includes Jest, Supertest, Vitest and Playwright.

records.title: How does Sreerag deploy and host his projects?
records.content: Deployment: LearnWithHupe runs on AWS EC2 with Nginx and PM2, with S3 and CloudFront for files, Cloudinary for media and Certbot for HTTPS. He also helped with server management for HRMS. The Warvox staging site is on Vercel. This assistant runs on a Cloudflare Worker that also serves the static site, and the Yexora website is a static export on Cloudflare with videos in R2. He also uses Docker and GitHub Actions. The records do not say he has run Kubernetes.

records.title: What AI work has Sreerag done?
records.content: AI work: this portfolio assistant (retrieval-augmented generation with Gemini, a Qdrant vector database, hybrid search with rank fusion, prompt design with safety rules and a measured evaluation); an MCP server with OAuth in a personal tracker app; and daily use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Google Antigravity) for scaffolding, review and testing. He is looking for work where he can use AI in products.

records.title: Has Sreerag worked on mobile apps?
records.content: Yes, on the backend and admin side, plus games. He built the backend, admin panel and server operations for LearnWithHupe, which is live on Google Play and the App Store, and he manages the Play Console and App Store Connect. He built its Phaser.js games, which run inside the Flutter app. The Flutter app itself was built by a separate Flutter developer, and Sreerag is not a Flutter specialist.

records.title: Has Sreerag worked in a team, and with whom?
records.content: Yes. At Carina Softlabs he works with the Team Lead and a separate Flutter developer, and he mentored three junior interns (two on Warvox, one on the PM tool): he assigned tasks, reviewed code and reported progress to the Team Lead. At Medlare he worked in an Agile sprint process. HRMS and the PM tool are team projects. As a freelancer he works directly with clients.

records.title: Has Sreerag led or taught anyone?
records.content: He has mentored three junior interns at Carina Softlabs (assigning tasks, reviewing their code and reporting their progress to the technical lead), and he taught web development basics in the Upthrust training programme. He works in a team led by the Team Lead.

records.title: What has Sreerag shipped to real users?
records.content: Live for real users: LearnWithHupe on Google Play and the App Store (small usage so far, marketing not started); Upthrust at theupthrust.com; the Carina Softlabs website at carinasoftlabs.com; the Yexora IT Solutions website; this assistant; and the open source packages on npm (Erris and Norix). In live internal use: HRMS (about 80 people) and the PM tool and Sales tool. Not publicly launched yet: Warvox.

records.title: What numbers can Sreerag point to?
records.content: Numbers from his records: more than 120 REST endpoints in the LearnWithHupe backend (about 60 for the admin panel); up to 10 children per parent account in LearnWithHupe; HRMS used by about 80 people; Warvox content in 11 languages (English plus 10); 4 packages published for Erris at version 1.0.2; the Norix CLI at version 1.16.2 with 5 releases; three junior interns mentored. The retrieval and answer results of this assistant are in its own project records. The records do not contain response-time improvements in milliseconds or any revenue figures.

records.title: How many users does Sreerag's work have, and what about revenue?
records.content: Usage is small and early: LearnWithHupe has been live on the two app stores for about two months (as of Nov 2026) and the company has not started marketing it; Warvox is not publicly launched; HRMS is used by about 80 colleagues; Norix had about 6 weekly and 26 monthly downloads in late Oct 2026; Erris downloads are small. The records contain no revenue figures, so he cannot give any.

records.title: What are the hardest problems Sreerag has solved?
records.content: Harder problems he describes: keeping LearnWithHupe subscriptions correct when renewals and refunds happen in the stores (the store is the source of truth, with scheduled re-checks); a duplicate-notification race that wrongly rejected real purchases; Google plan-change tokens that broke the link to the original subscriber; a translation pipeline for 11 languages in Warvox with retries and change detection; a 3D model viewer that fits any model into a card; and cutting the cost of text-to-speech in LearnWithHupe by generating voices once. Each has its own record with the details.

records.title: What patterns show in Sreerag's engineering decisions?
records.content: Patterns in his documented decisions: he treats the provider as the source of truth and re-checks instead of trusting local state (LearnWithHupe billing); he reduces cost by doing work once (pre-generated voices in LearnWithHupe, content-hash change detection in Warvox, an embedding cache in this assistant); he keeps libraries small and independent (Erris core with no dependencies and no HTTP); he follows standards (RFC 9457 in Erris); he adds regression tests when he fixes a bug; and he protects private data by design. This is a reading of the decision records, not a separate claim.

records.title: Comparing Sreerag's backend work on LearnWithHupe and Warvox
records.content: LearnWithHupe backend: a modular Express backend with more than 120 REST endpoints for parents, children and the admin panel; Google and Apple sign-in; child profiles and progress sync in transactions; subscription billing against Google Play and the App Store with scheduled re-checks; promo codes; ZIP uploads of learning activities; Socket.io; account safety and deletion; AWS servers. Its hard problems are about money and data correctness. Warvox backend: an Express backend with admin APIs and role-based access control; server-side Stripe checkout with webhook signature verification; a translation pipeline (a queue, AWS Translate, retries and change detection) that serves 11 languages; and content and forum features. Its hard problems are about content and languages. This comparison is drawn from the records for both projects; the records hold more detail on the LearnWithHupe backend.

records.title: What frontend work has Sreerag done?
records.content: Frontend work: the LearnWithHupe admin panel (React 19, TypeScript, Vite), the Upthrust website, the HRMS employee screens (profile, dashboard, attendance, leaves, calendar, policies, SOP and complaints), the Warvox website with a 3D model viewer, the PM tool and Sales tool dashboards and projects pages (Next.js), the Carina Softlabs website in Angular 22 with SSR, the Yexora site with a 3D scene, and this assistant's front end.

records.title: What backend work has Sreerag done?
records.content: Backend work: the LearnWithHupe backend (authentication, billing, progress, admin APIs, uploads, real-time); the Warvox backend (admin APIs, role-based access, Stripe checkout, translation pipeline); HRMS APIs for complaints, policies and the employee profile; the Upthrust backend; the PM tool and Sales tool backend (tasks, milestones, sprints and notifications); REST APIs at Medlare; and the Cloudflare Worker behind this assistant.

records.title: Which admin panels and CMS has Sreerag built?
records.content: Admin panels he built: the LearnWithHupe admin panel (curriculum with draft, published and archived states, analytics, subscription management and promo-code campaigns); the Upthrust CMS where staff add content that appears on the public site, plus its LMS; the Warvox admin backend with role-based access for content, translations and models; and the Carina Softlabs website admin panel, which he migrated to Angular 22.

records.title: What cost-saving and efficiency decisions has Sreerag made?
records.content: Cost and efficiency decisions: in LearnWithHupe he generated the text-to-speech voices once with a script and stored the audio instead of calling the paid API on every request; in Warvox a content hash lets the translation pipeline skip fields that did not change; in this assistant an in-memory cache avoids embedding repeated questions again and a second model is used as a fallback.

records.title: Has Sreerag written documentation or design papers?
records.content: He wrote the technical documentation for LearnWithHupe, a written design RFC for Erris (Erris-RFC-0001), and the setup, decision and evaluation notes of this assistant (a decision log with the reasons for each choice).

records.title: How do the Erris and Norix projects differ?
records.content: Erris is a solo open source library for typed, transport-neutral error contracts in JavaScript and TypeScript, published as four npm packages at version 1.0.2, with a design RFC, CI and CodeQL. Norix (norix-cli) is a command line tool that scans a Node.js repository offline and reports frameworks, databases, authentication, architecture insights and project health, at version 1.16.2. Both are MIT licensed, started around Aug 2026, and have small download numbers so far.

records.title: Has Sreerag worked with Docker, Kubernetes or microservices?
records.content: Docker is on his skills list and he runs production servers with Nginx and PM2 on AWS EC2. The records do not say he has run Kubernetes or built a microservice system, so he does not claim it. What he has done instead: deployed and operated LearnWithHupe on AWS, helped with HRMS servers, and set up CI with GitHub Actions.

records.title: How can a recruiter hire or contact Sreerag?
records.content: The quickest way is email: psreerag69@gmail.com. LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/sreerag-p. GitHub: github.com/sreeragpariyarath. He is open to full stack developer roles and forward deployed engineer roles, and open to relocating. He currently works as a Full Stack Developer at Carina Softlabs in Indore.

records.title: Personal tracker app with a ChatGPT connector
records.content: A personal web app with owner-only login, built in Oct 2026 with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript and MongoDB Atlas, deployed on Vercel. It keeps a follow-up queue, a searchable ledger and a CSV import. It also has a read-only MCP server with OAuth, so ChatGPT can read it, and a create action that shows a preview, needs approval and keeps an audit history. Auth0 with Google handles sign-in, and it has automated tests for auth, the MCP tools and previews. It also runs cron jobs and sends Firebase push notifications, so it messages the owner when it is time to follow up on a job application. It is private and for the owner only for now; a phase 2 is planned so other people can use it too.
